requirement:
HC's issue-content implementation can cache a fetched issue snapshot with a
fetch time and an application-selected TTL. When caching is enabled, reads
within the TTL reuse that snapshot. After expiry, a network-enabled read obtains
a refreshed snapshot before returning contents, or reports a refresh failure.
The returned contents, formatter, and fingerprint remain based on the same
snapshot.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.cache` has four testable obligations:
- Reads within the TTL reuse the cached snapshot when caching is enabled.
- After expiry, a network-enabled read refreshes the snapshot before returning contents.
- After expiry, a failed refresh is reported as a refresh failure.
- The returned contents, formatter and fingerprint all come from the same snapshot.

The `references` tool shows no `{test}` or `{impl}` sites for this requirement. A case-insensitive search of the repository for "ttl" found no code or test about snapshot TTL caching. The only relevant text is the `{fixme}` block on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]`.

That `{fixme}` names `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.cache` and `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`, which is open. Its body says tests do not yet cover reuse, expiry refresh or failure, or snapshot-consistent formatting and fingerprinting. That matches the gaps I found. It also notes that the CLI issue-state cache is a separate interface.

So the tests leave every obligation untested. No exemption applies, because TTL expiry and refresh are conditional behavior. The `{fixme}` acknowledges all of these gaps, and its issue is open.
